@gwOutcomeExpired.description: How a task ended, inside gwStepFinished: expired. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwOutcomeFailed.description: How a task ended, inside gwStepFinished: failed. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwOutcomeOffline.description: How a task ended, inside gwStepFinished: offline. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwOutcomePartial.description: How a task ended, inside gwStepFinished: partial. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwOutcomeReplaced.description: How a task ended, inside gwStepFinished: replaced. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwOutcomeStopped.description: How a task ended, inside gwStepFinished: stopped. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusBackground.description: A phone's status line: an agent works on a background display; work is "agent · task". Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusIdle.description: A phone's status line: nothing runs on it. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusInControl.description: A phone's status line: the person took over. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusInControlPaused.description: A phone's status line: the person took over and the agent waits. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusLocked.description: A phone's status line: the phone is locked. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusLockedTask.description: A phone's status line: the phone is locked and a task waits. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusNeedsSetup.description: A phone's status line in the demo: it is connected but not ready. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusNeedsYou.description: A phone's status line: an agent asked the person to do something (title is its reason). Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusOffline.description: A phone's status line in the sidebar and tiles: the phone is offline. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusOfflineDetail.description: A phone's status line: offline, with why (from the phone's driver, in English). Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusReconnecting.description: A phone's status line: offline while a task waits for it to come back. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStatusWaiting.description: A phone's status line: an approval waits (title is the approval's, gwAskPay and the like). Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepAskedTakeOver.description: A step: the agent asked the person to do something on the phone; reason is the agent's own words. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepAskedYou.description: A step: the agent asked the person a question, in quotes. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepBlocked.description: A step that a policy rule refused; rule is the rule's name (rulePayments and the like). Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepConnected.description: A task's first step: the agent connected to the phone for this task. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepCopiedFrom.description: A step: the agent copied files from the phone; names is gwFilesList or empty. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepCopiedTo.description: A step: the agent copied files to the phone; names is gwFilesList or empty. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepFailed.description: A step that failed. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepFinished.description: A task's last step: how the agent said it ended (gwOutcomeDone and the like). Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

gwStepListedFolder: Listed the phone's Pinky folder ({count} files)

@gwStepListedFolder.description: A step: the agent listed the files in the phone's Pinky folder. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepOutside.description: A step outside what the person allowed the agent. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepUnlocked.description: A step: the phone was unlocked from this computer with its saved PIN. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepWaited.description: A step: the agent waited for this text to show on the screen. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepWaiting.description: A step that waits for the person's approval; action is gwDoTap and the like.

@gwStepYouAllowed.description: A step of the demo's fake gateway: the person allowed an action. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepYouDenied.description: A step of the demo's fake gateway: the person denied an action. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepYouStopped.description: A step of the demo's fake gateway: the person stopped the task. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepYouTookOver.description: A step of the demo's fake gateway: the person took over. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepYourNote.description: The second line of a step: the note the person gave with an answer, in quotes. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

gwUnlockDetail: {agent} is waiting for the phone to unlock · {task}

@gwUnlockDetail.description: The second line of the unlock card. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwUnlockTitle.description: The title of the card that asks the person to unlock a locked phone an agent waits for. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@listMany.description: Three or more names in a sentence: rest is the names before the last, joined with listSeparator.

@listPair.description: Two names in a sentence, as "Can use Dinely and Chatter".

@listSeparator.description: Joins the names of a list before its last one (see listMany).

@menuPhones.description: The menu bar's menu of the app's pages and Stop all.

@menuStopAll.description: Phones menu: stops every agent on every phone.

@mirrorAgentScreenLabel.description: The accessibility label of the mirror while it shows the agent's own screen: the hidden second screen it works on in the background. agent is the agent's name, or "The agent" (agentGenericStart); phone is the phone's name.

@mirrorCallKey.description: A verb phrase that completes the toast "Couldn't …: <error>" (zh: 无法…：<error>) when a key pressed on the mirror cannot reach the phone. key is the phone's name for the key, in English: back, home, enter, tab, delete, escape, dpad_up, page_down…

@mirrorCallPaste.description: A verb phrase that completes the toast "Couldn't …: <error>" (zh: 无法…：<error>) when ⌘V on the mirror cannot paste the Mac's clipboard on the phone.

@mirrorCallTouch.description: A verb phrase that completes the toast "Couldn't …: <error>" (zh: 无法…：<error>) when a click, drag or scroll on the mirror cannot reach the phone.

@mirrorCallType.description: A verb phrase that completes the toast "Couldn't …: <error>" (zh: 无法…：<error>) when text typed on the mirror cannot reach the phone.

@mirrorConnecting.description: Under a spinner over the mirror while the phone's live picture connects.

@mirrorDecoderSoftware.description: Settings › Advanced in Developer mode, the Video row: how a mirror decodes without a hardware decoder, in place of a hardware decoder's name such as videotoolbox (see mirrorDecoderStats).

@mirrorDecoderStats.description: Settings › Advanced in Developer mode, the Video row: adds a playing mirror to the line. line is the line so far (FFmpeg's libavcodec version and the mirrors before); device is the phone's ID; decoder is mirrorDecoderSoftware or a hardware decoder's name; fps is pictures per second; latency is the time from a packet's arrival to its picture.

@mirrorLocked.description: A pill over the dimmed mirror of a locked phone. phone is the phone's name. One line over the phone's picture: keep it short.

@mirrorLockedTile.description: The same pill over a locked phone's tile in All phones, which can be 168 points wide.

@mirrorNoPicture.description: Over the mirror when the phone's live picture fails. detail is the error, in English.

@mirrorOffline.description: Over the mirror when the phone disconnected.

@mirrorScreenLabel.description: The accessibility label of the mirror, the phone's live picture, where clicks, scrolls and typing reach the phone. phone is the phone's name.

@mirrorStreamEnded.description: Over the mirror when the phone's live picture stopped; it connects again by itself.

mirrorUnsupported: This phone has no live picture.

@mirrorUnsupported.description: Over the mirror of a phone that cannot stream its screen.

@needsAddNote.description: Link on a handoff card that opens a field for a note to the agent.

@needsAllow.description: Primary button that allows the step once: on approval cards and in the floating approval panel.

@needsAllowTask.description: Item of More options: allow steps like this one until the agent's task ends.

@needsAlwaysAllow.description: Item of More options: never ask again for steps like this one. kind says what they are, from the rule that asked (zh 付款, 发送消息, 更改设置, 执行所有操作), or "this kind" (zh 此类操作) when no rule is named.

@needsAlwaysAllowIn.description: Item of More options on an approval card: never ask again for steps like this one in this app. kind says what they are, from the rule that asked (zh 付款, 发送消息, 更改设置, 执行所有操作); app is the app's name.

@needsAndTasksLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Phones page's right-hand column, which holds the Needs you cards and the Tasks.

@needsApprove.description: Primary button on an agent's first-connection card: lets the agent use the phones as chosen above it.

@needsApproveNoApps.description: The tooltip of the disabled Approve button on a first-connection card, when "Only the apps I choose" is chosen and no app is named yet.

@needsDecline.description: Button (or link) on a handoff card: tells the agent the person won't do what it asked.

@needsDeclineTooltip.description: The tooltip of Decline on a handoff card.

@needsDeny.description: Button that denies an approval or an agent's first connection: on Needs you cards and in the floating approval panel.

needsDenyNotePlaceholder: Why not, or what to do instead

@needsDenyNotePlaceholder.description: The placeholder of the note field after Deny with a note, on an approval card: why the person said no, or what the agent should do instead.

@needsDenyWithNote.description: Item of More options: opens a field for a note to the agent, then Deny sends it with the answer.

@needsDone.description: Button on a handoff card: the person did what the agent asked, and the phone goes back to the agent, with the note if there is one.

@needsDoneTooltip.description: The tooltip of Done on a handoff card.

@needsFirstConnection.description: The small line above a card's title when an agent connects for the first time and asks to use the phones. Other cards show the phone and app there, as "Pixel 9 · Dinely".

needsHandoffHowTo: Do it on the phone and click Done, or take over to do it here.

@needsHandoffHowTo.description: A handoff card: the agent asked the person to do something on the phone (its request is the card's title). Done and Take over are the card's buttons.

needsHandoffInControl: You're in control. Click Done to hand the phone back to {agent}.

@needsHandoffInControl.description: A handoff card (the agent asked the person to do something on the phone, its request is the title) after the person took over. Done is the card's button (needsDone).

@needsHandoffLocked.description: A handoff card on a locked phone that this computer cannot unlock. how is a sentence that says how to unlock it, ending with needsThenClickDone.

how.example: Unlock it on the phone, then click Done.

needsHandoffLockedHere: The phone is locked. Unlocking it here hands it back to {agent}. If you unlock it on the phone, click Done when you're finished.

@needsHandoffLockedHere.description: A handoff card on a locked phone that this computer can unlock, under the Unlock with Touch ID button. Done is the card's button (needsDone).

needsHandoffNotePlaceholder: What you did, or what to do next

@needsHandoffNotePlaceholder.description: The placeholder of the note field on a handoff card: what the person did on the phone, or what the agent should do next.

@needsLetAgent.description: On an agent's first-connection card: the label above (and the accessibility label of) the menu of what the agent may do. In English it reads on into the choice: "Let Claude Code" + "All apps except blocked ones", "Only the apps I choose", "Browse and read, never commit" or "Watch only".

@needsMoreOptions.description: Link under Deny and Allow, on approval cards and in the floating approval panel, that opens a menu: Allow for this task, Always allow …, Take over, Deny with a note.

@needsNoteFor.description: The label above (and the accessibility label of) the field where the person writes a note to the agent: on handoff and approval cards and in the floating approval panel.

@needsSection.description: The heading (and accessibility label) of the cards that wait for the person (approvals, handoffs, locked phones): in the right-hand column and in the menu bar flyout.

needsTakeOverTooltip: Do it here, in the mirror

@needsTakeOverTooltip.description: The tooltip of Take over on a handoff card: the person does what the agent asked in the app's live picture of the phone.

@needsThenClickDone.description: Ends the sentence that says how to unlock a phone on a handoff card ("Unlock it on the phone, then click Done."): it starts with a comma and ends the sentence. Done is the card's button (needsDone).

@pairingAddrField.description: Pair with a code: the label above the field for the address the phone shows (as 192.168.1.20:37123), and the field's accessibility label.

pairingAddrInvalid: Enter the IP address and port the phone shows, like 192.168.1.20:37123.

@pairingAddrInvalid.description: Pair with a code: the error under the form when the address typed is not an IP address and port.

@pairingBusy.description: Pair with a code: next to a spinner, right of the Pair button, while Pinky pairs.

pairingCodeDetail: On the phone, open Developer options › Wireless debugging and tap Pair device with pairing code. Enter what it shows.

@pairingCodeDetail.description: Pair with a code: the line under the heading. Developer options, Wireless debugging and Pair device with pairing code are Android's own names: use those of Android's Simplified Chinese settings.

@pairingCodeField.description: Pair with a code: the label above the field for the six-digit pairing code the phone shows, and the field's accessibility label.

pairingCodeIncomplete: Enter the six-digit code the phone shows.

@pairingCodeIncomplete.description: Pair with a code: the error under the form when the code typed has fewer than six digits.

@pairingCodePlaceholder.description: Pair with a code: the placeholder of the pairing code field, a narrow field.

@pairingCodeTitle.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the heading of the form that pairs with the address and the six-digit code the phone shows.

pairingErrNoAdb: This computer can't pair phones over Wi-Fi: Pinky found no Android tools (adb) to pair with. Use a USB cable instead.

@pairingErrNoAdb.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the error when this computer has no Android tools (adb) to pair with.

@pairingErrOther.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the error when pairing failed for another reason. detail is the error, in English.

pairingErrTimeout: The phone didn't answer in time. Check that it's on the same Wi-Fi as this computer and that Wireless debugging is on, then try again.

@pairingErrTimeout.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the error when the phone did not answer in time. Wireless debugging is Android's setting.

pairingErrUnreachable: Couldn't reach the phone at that address. Check the IP address and port under Pair device with pairing code; they change each time it opens.

@pairingErrUnreachable.description: Pair with a code: the error when nothing answered at the address typed. Pair device with pairing code is Android's own name.

pairingErrUnsupported: Pairing over Wi-Fi isn't available here. Use a USB cable instead.

@pairingErrUnsupported.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the error when the phone's driver cannot pair over Wi-Fi.

pairingErrWrongCode: The pairing code didn't match. Use the code the phone shows now; it changes each time you open Pair device with pairing code.

@pairingErrWrongCode.description: Pair with a code: the error when the pairing code typed was wrong. Pair device with pairing code is Android's own name.

@pairingGettingCode.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the status line, next to a spinner, while Pinky gets the QR code from the gateway.

@pairingNoCode.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: in place of the QR code, under an alert icon, when getting one failed.

@pairingPair.description: Add phone: the button that pairs with the code typed, in the Android form "Pair with a code" and in the iPhone step.

@pairingPaired.description: A notice once a phone paired over Wi-Fi; its page opens. name is the phone's name.

@pairingPairedPhone.description: A notice once a phone paired over Wi-Fi, when its name is unknown.

pairingQRDetail: On the phone, open Developer options › Wireless debugging and tap Pair device with QR code, then scan this code. Keep the phone on the same Wi-Fi as this computer.

@pairingQRDetail.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the line under the heading, above the QR code. Developer options, Wireless debugging and Pair device with QR code are Android's own names: use those of Android's Simplified Chinese settings.

@pairingQRDrawError.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the status line when Pinky could not draw the QR code. detail is the error, in English.

pairingQRLabel: QR code to scan in Wireless debugging › Pair device with QR code

@pairingQRLabel.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the accessibility label of the QR code. Wireless debugging and Pair device with QR code are Android's own names.

pairingSlowHint: Taking a while? This computer and the phone must be on the same Wi-Fi. If the phone says it paired and nothing happens here, adb may have stopped seeing the network: quit other Android tools and run adb kill-server, then try again.

@pairingSlowHint.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: under the status line when the phone has not paired after 30 seconds. adb is Android's tool and adb kill-server a command: both stay as they are.

@pairingTitle.description: Add phone › Pair over Wi-Fi: the heading of the step that pairs an Android phone over Wi-Fi with a QR code.

pairingUnsupported: This gateway can't pair phones over Wi-Fi. Connect the phone with a USB cable instead.

@pairingUnsupported.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the line under the heading when the gateway Pinky uses cannot pair phones.

@pairingUseCode.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the link that switches from the QR code to typing the address and six-digit code the phone shows.

@pairingUseQR.description: Pair with a code: the link that switches back to the QR code.

@pairingUseUSB.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the link that goes back to connecting the phone with a USB cable.

pairingWaiting: Waiting for the phone to scan the code…

@pairingWaiting.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the status line under the QR code, next to a spinner, while Pinky waits for the phone to scan it.

@panelActionsLikeThis.description: Stands for the rule's name in panelAllowedTaskDetail and panelAlwaysAllowedDetail when the approval names no rule.

panelAgentAllowed: {agent} can use your phones. Change what it may do in Settings › Agents.

@panelAgentAllowed.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Allowed, after the person approved an agent's first connection. Settings › Agents is the Settings section that lists the agents.

@panelAgentDenied.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Denied, after the person denied an agent's first connection.

@panelAllowed.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Approve on an agent's first connection.

@panelAllowedOnce.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Allow.

panelAllowedOnceDetail: Pinky checks the button is still on screen, then taps it.

@panelAllowedOnceDetail.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Allowed once: what happens on the phone next.

@panelAllowedTask.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Allow for this task.

panelAllowedTaskDetail: {rule} in {app} are allowed until this task ends.

@panelAllowedTaskDetail.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Allowed for this task. rule is the name of the rule that asked (zh 付款, 发送消息, 更改设置, 所有操作), or panelActionsLikeThis; app is the app's name, or panelThisApp.

@panelAlwaysAllowed.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Always allow ….

panelAlwaysAllowedDetail: {rule} in {app} no longer ask. Change it in Settings.

@panelAlwaysAllowedDetail.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Always allowed: Pinky won't ask the person about these steps again. rule is the name of the rule that asked (zh 付款, 发送消息, 更改设置, 所有操作), or panelActionsLikeThis; app is the app's name, or panelThisApp.

@panelCancel.description: Button in the floating approval panel's note editor: back to the approval without denying it.

@panelDeclined.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Decline on a handoff.

@panelDenied.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Deny, on an approval or an agent's first connection.

panelDeniedDetail: Nothing was tapped. {agent} was told no.

@panelDeniedDetail.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Denied, after the person denied a step.

panelDeniedDetailNote: Nothing was tapped. {agent} was told no, with your note: “{note}”

@panelDeniedDetailNote.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Denied, after the person denied a step with a note. note is the person's own words.

@panelDeniesIn.description: Top right of the floating approval panel: the approval is denied by itself when this time runs out. duration is as "42 s" (zh 42 秒).

@panelDenyWithNote.description: Primary button in the floating approval panel's note editor: denies the approval and sends the note to the agent. Half of the 360-point panel's width.

@panelEndsIn.description: Top right of the floating approval panel for a handoff (the agent asked the person to do something): the request ends when this time runs out. duration is as "4 min 10 s" (zh 4 分 10 秒).

@panelHandedBack.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Done on a handoff: the phone went back to the agent.

@panelHandedBackDetail.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Handed back.

@panelNext.description: The accessibility label of the floating approval panel's right arrow.

@panelPosition.description: The floating approval panel's pager, between its two arrows: which of the waiting approvals it shows. Keep it short.

@panelPrevious.description: The accessibility label of the floating approval panel's left arrow.

@panelShotLabel.description: The accessibility label of the floating approval panel's picture: the part of the phone's screen around what the agent wants to tap, with that element outlined.

@panelThisApp.description: Stands for the app's name in panelAllowedTaskDetail and panelAlwaysAllowedDetail when the approval names no app.

@panelToldNo.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Declined: the agent learned that the person won't do what it asked.

@panelWaitingApprovals.description: The accessibility label of the floating approval panel's pager (previous, "1 of 2", next) when several approvals wait.

@panelWindowTitle.description: The title of the floating approval panel's window. The panel has no title bar; screen readers and window lists read it.

@panelWithNote.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation after a handoff was answered with a note: text is the confirmation's sentence (panelHandedBackDetail or panelToldNo), note the person's own words.

text.example: Claude Code goes on from here.

@phoneAddPhone.description: Primary button on the Phones page before any phone is added: opens Add phone.

@phoneAgentScreen.description: Choice of the switch under the mirror while an agent works on a hidden second screen: the mirror shows the agent's screen.

@phoneAllPhones.description: The Phones page's title when it shows every phone as live tiles.

phoneBackgroundDesc: Agents use a hidden second screen, so the phone stays yours and can stay locked. From the next task.

@phoneBackgroundDesc.description: Under Work in the background in ⋯ under the mirror: what the switch does, and that it applies from the agent's next task.

phoneBackgroundUnsupported: This phone can't give agents a second screen.

@phoneBackgroundUnsupported.description: Under Work in the background in ⋯, when the phone can't do it (the switch is disabled).

phoneBannerHandBackHint: Hand back to let agents use this phone again.

@phoneBannerHandBackHint.description: The banner over the mirror, after the bold phoneBannerInControl, when no agent waits: Hand back is the banner's button.

@phoneBannerInControl.description: The bold start of the banner over the mirror while the person controls the phone; the rest follows in normal weight (phoneBannerPaused or phoneBannerHandBackHint). English ends with a space before the rest.

@phoneBannerPaused.description: The banner over the mirror, after the bold phoneBannerInControl: the agent waits until the person hands the phone back.

@phoneBannerWaits.description: The banner over the mirror, after the bold phoneBannerYourTurn. reason is the agent's own words, what it asked the person to do (in English with a lower-case first letter).

@phoneBannerYourTurn.description: The bold start of the banner over the mirror when the agent asked the person to do something on the phone; phoneBannerWaits follows in normal weight. English ends with a space before the rest.

@phoneConnected.description: All phones, next to the title: how many phones are online.

@phoneHandBack.description: Button that gives the phone back to the agents after the person took over: on the banner over the mirror and on All phones tiles.

@phoneKeyBack.description: Android's Back key, a button under the mirror (accessibility label and tooltip).

@phoneKeyHome.description: The phone's Home key, a button under the mirror (accessibility label and tooltip).

@phoneKeyRecents.description: Android's Recents key (recent apps), a button under the mirror (accessibility label and tooltip).

phoneKeysAgentScreen: {agent} works on its own screen. Show the phone's screen to use the phone.

@phoneKeysAgentScreen.description: The tooltip of the disabled keys under the mirror while it shows the agent's hidden second screen. "Phone's screen" is a choice of the switch next to them.

@phoneMoreControls.description: The accessibility label and tooltip of the ⋯ button under the mirror, which opens Take screenshot, Record screen, Rotate and Work in the background.

@phoneNeedsSetup.description: A phone's page when the phone is connected but can't be used yet (USB debugging off, not trusted); the system's reason shows under it.

@phoneNoPhones.description: The Phones page before any phone is added, above the Add phone button.

@phoneNoPicture.description: Toast after Take screenshot when the mirror has shown no picture of the phone yet.

@phoneNotConnected.description: Under phoneOffline when the system says nothing more, before the Reconnect link.

@phoneOffline.description: A phone's page when the phone is offline, under a phone outline.

@phoneOfflineCount.description: All phones, next to the title after phoneConnected and a " · ": how many phones are offline.

@phonePageTitle.description: The Phones page's title before any phone is added.

@phonePhoneScreen.description: Choice of the switch under the mirror while an agent works on a hidden second screen: the mirror shows the phone's own screen.

@phonePressKey.description: What failed, inside the toast "Couldn't press Back: <error>" (zh 无法按返回键：<error>). key is the key's name: phoneKeyBack, phoneKeyHome or phoneKeyRecents.

@phoneReconnect.description: Link on an offline phone's page: opens Add phone.

@phoneRecordScreen.description: Item of ⋯ under the mirror, shown disabled.

phoneRecordScreenTooltip: Agent tasks are recorded while Record the screen is on in Settings › Privacy

@phoneRecordScreenTooltip.description: The tooltip of the disabled Record screen item: recording happens through a setting. "Record the screen" is the switch's name in Settings › Privacy.

@phoneRotate.description: Item of ⋯ under the mirror, shown disabled: would rotate the phone's screen.

phoneRotateTooltip: Not in the gateway API yet

@phoneRotateTooltip.description: The tooltip of the disabled Rotate item.

@phoneScreenLabel.description: The accessibility label of the phone frame around the mirror, the live picture of the phone's screen.

@phoneScreenshotFailed.description: Toast when writing a screenshot to the Desktop failed. reason is the system's error, in English.

@phoneScreenshotName.description: The name of a screenshot file on the Desktop, before ".png": the phone, the date as 2026-11-07 and the time as 09.30.12 (dots: file names can't have colons).

@phoneScreenshotSaved.description: Toast after Take screenshot: the file's name on the Desktop (phoneScreenshotName and .png).

@phoneShow.description: The accessibility label of a one-line task row and of an All phones tile: a click shows that phone.

@phoneShowOnMirror.description: The accessibility label of the switch under the mirror between the agent's screen and the phone's.

@phoneTakeOver.description: Button or menu item that gives the person control of the phone in the mirror and pauses the agent: on handoff cards, in an approval's More options (card and floating panel), on the task card and on All phones tiles.

@phoneTakeScreenshot.description: Item of ⋯ under the mirror: saves the phone's screen as a picture on the Desktop.

@phoneWorkInBackground.description: The title (and the switch's accessibility label) of the row in ⋯ under the mirror that lets agents work on a hidden second screen.

@phoneWorksInBackground.description: A phone's page, next to the title after the connection and a " · ": the agent works on a hidden second screen of the phone.

@pinCancel.description: The PIN form: the button that closes it without saving.

@pinChange.description: Next to "PIN saved": the link that opens the PIN form to type a new PIN.

@pinChangeLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Change link next to "PIN saved". name is the phone's name.

@pinErrRemove.description: A notice when the keychain could not remove the PIN. detail is the system's error, in English.

detail.example: keychain: user interaction is not allowed

@pinErrSave.description: The PIN form: the error when the keychain could not save the PIN. detail is the system's error, in English.

detail.example: keychain: user interaction is not allowed

pinErrShort: Enter the PIN or passcode that unlocks {name}: at least 4 characters.

@pinErrShort.description: The PIN form: the error when the PIN typed is shorter than 4 characters. name is the phone's name.

@pinFieldLabel.description: The PIN form: the accessibility label of the PIN field. name is the phone's name.

@pinPlaceholder.description: The PIN form: the placeholder of the secure field where the person types the phone's PIN or passcode.

@pinRemove.description: Next to "PIN saved": the link that removes the saved PIN.

@pinRemoveLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Remove link next to "PIN saved". name is the phone's name.

@pinRemovedToast.description: A notice after the PIN was removed. name is the phone's name.

@pinSave.description: The PIN form: the button that saves the PIN typed in the system's keychain.

@pinSaveLabel.description: The accessibility label of the button Save PIN…. name is the phone's name.

@pinSaveOpen.description: The small button that opens the PIN form, where no PIN is saved for the phone (Settings › Phones, the locked phone's card).

@pinSaved.description: Where a phone's PIN is saved (Settings › Phones and the locked phone's card): next to a lock icon, before the links Change and Remove.

@pinSavedToast.description: A notice after the PIN was saved. name is the phone's name.

platformUnlockKeepMac: Your PIN stays in your Mac's Keychain. Agents never see it.

@platformUnlockKeepMac.description: macOS: where a saved phone PIN is kept, under the PIN field.

platformUnlockKeepOther: Your PIN stays in your keyring. Agents never see it.

@platformUnlockKeepOther.description: Linux: where a saved phone PIN is kept, under the PIN field.

platformUnlockKeepWindows: Your PIN stays in Windows Credential Manager. Agents never see it.

@platformUnlockKeepWindows.description: Windows: where a saved phone PIN is kept, under the PIN field.

@platformUnlockMac.description: macOS: the button that unlocks a locked phone with its saved PIN, after Touch ID or the Mac's password.

@platformUnlockOther.description: Linux: the button that unlocks a locked phone with its saved PIN.

@platformUnlockWindows.description: Windows: the button that unlocks a locked phone with its saved PIN.

@recordingEnded.description: Over the recording's picture when it stopped without an error.

recordingGone: The recording is gone; the history limit may have removed it.

@recordingGone.description: Over the recording's picture when its file is missing. Settings › Privacy › Keep activity for deletes older recordings.

@recordingJumpHeading.description: The heading of the list of steps beside the recording: a click on a step plays the recording from that step.

@recordingJumpTo.description: The accessibility label of a step in the list beside the recording. at is where the step is in the recording, as 1:48; step is the step's text.

recordingNoMarks: No steps are marked in this recording.

@recordingNoMarks.description: In place of the list of steps beside a recording that has none marked.

@recordingPanelLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Watch recording panel.

@recordingPanelTitle.description: The title of the Watch recording panel. title is the task's title, as the agent wrote it.

@recordingPause.description: The accessibility label and tooltip of the player's icon button while the recording plays: pauses it.

@recordingPlay.description: The accessibility label and tooltip of the player's icon button while the recording is paused: plays it.

@recordingPlayAgain.description: The accessibility label and tooltip of the player's icon button once the recording has ended: plays it from the start.

@recordingPlayFailed.description: Over the recording's picture when it cannot play. detail is the error, in English.

detail.example: invalid data found when processing input

@recordingPlayerLabel.description: The accessibility label of the recording's picture, in a phone frame. title is the task's title, as the agent wrote it.

@recordingPosition.description: The accessibility label of the recording's timeline, a slider: a click jumps there, ← and → move by 5 s.

@recordingStepsLabel.description: The accessibility label of the list of steps beside the recording.

recordingUnsupported: This build of Pinky can't play recordings yet.

@recordingUnsupported.description: Over the recording's picture when this copy of Pinky cannot play recordings.

@recordingWatch.description: The button in a task's detail that plays the task's screen recording.

@replayMenuItem.description: An item of the ⋯ menu of a task that has a screen recording: shows the steps one at a time with their screenshots instead of the recording.

@replayNext.description: The accessibility label of Watch replay's › button, which shows the step after.

@replayNoSteps.description: Watch replay of a task that has no steps.

@replayPanelLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Watch replay panel.

@replayPanelTitle.description: The title of the Watch replay panel. title is the task's title, as the agent wrote it.

@replayPause.description: Watch replay's Play button while it plays: stops at the step shown.

@replayPlay.description: Watch replay's button that goes through the steps by itself, one every 1.5 s.

@replayPrevious.description: The accessibility label of Watch replay's ‹ button, which shows the step before.

@replayStepOf.description: Watch replay: the step shown, above its text. current is its number, total how many steps the task has.

replayTimelineHint: Each dot is a step. Larger dots are moments you were asked.

@replayTimelineHint.description: Under Watch replay's timeline, a row of dots, one per step; the dots of the steps where the agent asked the person are larger.

@replayWatch.description: The button in a task's detail that shows the task's steps one at a time with their screenshots, for a task without a screen recording.

replayWatchTooltip: Step by step, with the screenshots

@ruleActionAgentRequest.description: What the Agent request rule covers, inside "Always allow agent request in Dinely": the approvals the agent asks for itself.

@ruleActionCalls.description: What the Calls rule covers, inside "Always allow calls in Phone".

@ruleActionCommits.description: What the Commits rule covers, inside "Always allow commits in Dinely".

@ruleActionEveryAction.description: What the Every action rule covers, inside "Always allow every action in Dinely".

@ruleActionInstallsLinks.description: What the Installs and links rule covers, inside "Always allow installs and links in Chrome".

@ruleActionMessages.description: What the Messages rule covers, inside "Always allow messages in Chatter".

@ruleActionOther.description: What a rule of the person's own rules file covers, inside "Always allow … in Dinely": the rule's name with a lower-case first letter.

@ruleActionPayments.description: What the Payments rule covers, inside "Always allow payments in Dinely" (zh: 始终允许在 Dinely 中付款).

@ruleActionSettingsChanges.description: What the Settings changes rule covers, inside "Always allow settings changes in Settings".

@ruleActionThisKind.description: Inside "Always allow this kind" when the approval names no rule.

@ruleAgentRequest.description: The name of the rule of an approval the agent asked for itself (phone_request_approval).

@ruleAgentScope.description: The name of the rule that keeps an agent to what the person allowed it.

@ruleBlockedByYou.description: The name of the policy rule that denies the apps the person blocked.

@ruleCalls.description: The name of the policy rule that asks before calls.

@ruleCommits.description: The name of the policy rule that asks before deletions, posts and other commits.

@ruleCredentials.description: The name of the built-in rule that denies typing into password and one-time-code fields.

@ruleEveryAction.description: The name of the policy rule that asks before every action.

@ruleFiles.description: The name of the rule that asks before copying files to the phone.

@ruleFinanceApps.description: The name of the default rule that blocks finance apps.

@ruleInstallsLinks.description: The name of the policy rule that asks before installing apps and opening links that leave the app.

@ruleMessages.description: The name of the policy rule that asks before sending messages.

@rulePasswordManagers.description: The name of the default rule that blocks password managers.

@rulePayments.description: The name of the policy rule that asks before payments, as approvals and steps name it.

@ruleReadOnly.description: The name of the rule of Read-only mode.

@ruleSettingsChanges.description: The name of the policy rule that asks before changing a setting.

@ruleTaskApps.description: The name of the rule that keeps an agent to the apps of its task.

@scopeApps.description: A choice of what an agent may do: only the apps the person names.

@scopeEverything.description: A choice of what a new agent may do: any app but those blocked in Settings › Safety.

@scopeLineApps.description: Settings › Agents: an agent limited to these apps.

scopeLineEverything: Can use all apps except blocked ones

@scopeLineEverything.description: Settings › Agents: an agent that may use any app but the blocked ones.

@scopeLineNoApp.description: Settings › Agents: an agent limited to chosen apps, before any app is chosen.

scopeLineReadOnly: Can browse and read, never commit

@scopeLineReadOnly.description: Settings › Agents: an agent that may only look and read.

@scopeLineWatchOnly.description: Settings › Agents: an agent that may only see the screen.

@scopeReadOnly.description: A choice of what an agent may do: look and read, but never pay, send, delete or change anything.

@scopeWatchOnly.description: A choice of what an agent may do: see the screen, touch nothing.

@sentencePair.description: Joins two sentences in one line (zh: no space after 。).

@shotLabel.description: The accessibility label of a step's screenshot.

@shotLoading.description: In place of a step's screenshot while it loads.

@shotNone.description: In place of a step's screenshot when there is none.

@sidebarActivity.description: The sidebar row that opens Activity, the finished tasks.

@sidebarAddPhone.description: The sidebar row that opens Add phone.

@sidebarAllPhones.description: The sidebar row that shows every phone at once, as live tiles.

@sidebarPhoneRow.description: The accessibility label of a phone's sidebar row: its name and status line.

@sidebarPhones.description: The sidebar's heading above the list of phones.

@sidebarSettings.description: The sidebar row that opens Settings.

@sidebarStopAll.description: The sidebar's emergency button that stops every agent on every phone; its shortcut shows next to it.

stepAllowedNotUsed: Allowed, but the agent did not come back for it

@stepAllowedNotUsed.description: The second line of a step the person allowed but the agent never did.

@stepAsked.description: The second line of a handoff step: what the agent had asked, in its own words.

@stepCodeInternal.description: Why a step failed, inside stepFailedCode: internal.

@stepCodeInvalidArgument.description: Why a step failed, inside stepFailedCode: invalid argument.

@stepCodeLeaseHeld.description: Why a step failed, inside stepFailedCode: lease held.

@stepCodeNotFound.description: Why a step failed, inside stepFailedCode: not found.

@stepCodeScopeDenied.description: Why a step failed, inside stepFailedCode: scope denied.

@stepCodeUnsupported.description: Why a step failed, inside stepFailedCode: unsupported.

@stepFailedCode.description: The second line of a step that failed; reason is stepCodeNotFound and the like.

@stepMayHaveHappened.description: The second line of a step whose result is uncertain.

stepNotDoneInControl: Not done: you were in control

@stepNotDoneInControl.description: The second line of a step that never ran while the person was in control.

stepNotDoneStale: Not done: the screen changed while it waited

@stepNotDoneStale.description: The second line of an approved step that never ran because the screen changed.

@stepNotDoneStopped.description: The second line of a step that never ran because the task was stopped.

@stepNotDoneTookOver.description: The second line of a step that never ran because the person took over.

@stepPhoneLocked.description: The second line of a step that failed because the phone was locked.

@stepPhoneOffline.description: The second line of a step that failed because the phone went offline.

@stepWaiting.description: A task card's step that waits for the person's approval; action is what it would do (gwDoTap and the like).

@stepYouAgreed.description: A step: the person agreed to the agent's question, in quotes.

@stepYouAnswered.description: A step the person answered, while the action runs.

@stepYouDeclined.description: A step: the person declined what the agent asked them to do (a handoff).

@stepYouHandedBack.description: A step: the person did what the agent asked and handed the phone back.

@stepYouSaidNo.description: A step: the person said no to the agent's question, in quotes.

@tasksDetails.description: Developer mode: the title of the row at the bottom of a task card, whose switch shows the tool calls behind the steps.

@tasksDeveloperModeOn.description: Developer mode: under Details at the bottom of a task card, why the row is there.

tasksEarlierSteps: {count, plural, one {# earlier step} other {# earlier steps}}

@tasksEarlierSteps.description: Above a task card's last steps: how many earlier steps are not shown.

@tasksNoToolCalls.description: Developer mode: in place of a task's tool calls before the agent made any.

tasksNone: No tasks running. Ask your agent to use a phone.

@tasksNone.description: In place of the Tasks list when no agent is working on any phone.

@tasksRowDone.description: The short state at the end of a one-line task row: the task is finished.

@tasksRowEnded.description: The short state at the end of a one-line task row: the task ended after the person said no.

@tasksRowFailed.description: The short state at the end of a one-line task row: the task failed.

@tasksRowLocked.description: The short state at the end of a one-line task row: the phone is locked.

@tasksRowPaused.description: The short state at the end of a one-line row of another phone's task: the person took over.

@tasksRowStep.description: The short state at the end of a one-line task row while the agent works: the number of the step it is at.

@tasksRowStopped.description: The short state at the end of a one-line task row: the task was stopped.

@tasksRowWaiting.description: The short state at the end of a one-line task row: the agent waits for the person.

@tasksSection.description: The heading (and accessibility label) of the agents' tasks in the Phones page's right-hand column.

@tasksShowTechnicalDetails.description: The accessibility label of the Details switch on a task card: shows the tool calls in place of the steps.

@tasksStatusDone.description: A task card's status: the agent finished the task.

@tasksStatusEnded.description: A task card's status: the task ended after the person said no to one of its steps.

@tasksStatusFailed.description: A task card's status: the task failed.

@tasksStatusLocked.description: A task card's status, next to a dot: the phone is locked and the agent waits for it to be unlocked.

@tasksStatusPaused.description: A task card's status: the person took over the phone and the agent is paused.

@tasksStatusStopped.description: A task card's status: the task was stopped.

@tasksStatusWaiting.description: A task card's status: the agent waits for the person to answer an approval or a request.

@tasksStatusWorking.description: A task card's status, next to a pulsing dot: the agent is at work.

@tasksStepWithShot.description: The accessibility label of a task card's step that has a screenshot, which a click shows under the step. step is the step's text, as the list shows it.

@tasksStop.description: Red button that stops the agent's task: on the task card and on the All phones tiles.

@timeHours.description: A duration of an hour or more. minutes has two digits. Joined with no-break spaces.

@timeMinutes.description: A duration under an hour. seconds has two digits. Joined with no-break spaces.

@timeSeconds.description: A duration under a minute, as task cards and Activity show it. Joined with a no-break space so it never wraps.

@toastCouldNot.description: A toast when a call to the gateway fails: action is a verb phrase such as callTakeOver (zh: 接管), error the gateway's error in English.

@unlockBusy.description: The unlock button while it unlocks the phone; it reads "Unlock with Touch ID" (or the platform's word) otherwise.

@unlockCallWhat.description: Fills "Couldn't …: <error>" (zh: 无法…：<error>), a notice when unlocking a phone fails: a verb phrase.

@unlockEnd.description: Ends the hints that say how to unlock a phone on it (the unlockOnPhone messages) when nothing follows them: a full stop.

unlockErrNoPIN: No PIN is saved for {name}. Save it in Settings › Phones.

@unlockErrNoPIN.description: A notice when unlocking failed because no PIN is saved for the phone. name is the phone's name.

unlockErrNoPad: Pinky couldn't get to {name}'s passcode screen, so it entered nothing. Try again, or unlock it on the phone.

@unlockErrNoPad.description: A notice when Pinky could not reach the phone's passcode screen, so it typed nothing. name is the phone's name.

unlockErrNoUnlock: Unlocking from this computer isn't available. Unlock {name} on the phone.

@unlockErrNoUnlock.description: A notice when the gateway cannot unlock phones. name is the phone's name.

@unlockErrOffline.description: A notice when unlocking failed because the phone is offline. name is the phone's name.

@unlockErrOther.description: A notice when unlocking failed for another reason. name is the phone's name; detail is the error, in English.

unlockErrUnsupported: {name} can't be unlocked from this computer. Unlock it on the phone.

@unlockErrUnsupported.description: A notice when this phone cannot be unlocked from the computer. name is the phone's name.

unlockErrWrongPIN: The saved PIN didn't unlock {name}. To keep the phone from locking you out, Pinky won't try it again until you unlock the phone yourself or change the PIN in Settings › Phones.

@unlockErrWrongPIN.description: A notice when the phone refused its saved PIN. Pinky stops trying it, as phones lock out, or erase themselves, after repeated wrong PINs. name is the phone's name; Settings › Phones is Pinky's Settings page.

unlockFromHere: Unlock it from here when you or an agent need it.

@unlockFromHere.description: The locked phone's card, when its PIN is saved: above the unlock button. The card is in a narrow side panel.

@unlockLocked.description: The title of the card on a locked phone's side panel, next to a lock icon, and the card's accessibility label. name is the phone's name.

unlockNotAvailable: Unlocking from this computer is not available on this system.

@unlockNotAvailable.description: Where the system has no keychain Pinky can use, so phones cannot be unlocked from this computer: in the PIN form's place, and as a notice when unlocking fails.

@unlockNotNow.description: The locked phone's card: the quiet button that hides the card for this phone.

@unlockNotNowLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Not now button on the locked phone's card. name is the phone's name.

@unlockOnPhone.description: The locked phone's card: how to unlock it when this computer cannot. end is a full stop (unlockEnd), or ", then click Done." when the card in Needs you has a Done button, in the app's language.

unlockOnPhoneNotAvailable: Unlocking from this computer is not available on this system. Unlock it on the phone{end}

@unlockOnPhoneNotAvailable.description: The locked phone's card, when the system has no keychain Pinky can use. end as in unlockOnPhone.

unlockOnPhoneOff: Unlock it on the phone{end} Unlocking from this computer is off in Settings › Safety.

@unlockOnPhoneOff.description: The locked phone's card, when unlocking from this computer is turned off in Settings › Safety (the switch is named "Unlock from this computer"). end as in unlockOnPhone.

unlockOnPhoneSavePIN: Save the phone's PIN to unlock it from this computer, or unlock it on the phone{end}

@unlockOnPhoneSavePIN.description: The locked phone's card in Needs you, when no PIN is saved for it; the button Save PIN… follows. end as in unlockOnPhone.

unlockOnPhoneWrongPIN: The saved PIN didn't unlock it, so Pinky won't try it again. Unlock it on the phone{end} If its PIN changed, update it in Settings › Phones.

@unlockOnPhoneWrongPIN.description: The locked phone's card, after the phone refused its saved PIN: Pinky won't try it again. end as in unlockOnPhone.

unlockOrOnPhone: or unlock it on the phone

@unlockOrOnPhone.description: The locked phone's card in Needs you: the small line under the button that unlocks it from this computer.

unlockPitchMac: Save its PIN and you can unlock it from this computer with Touch ID when an agent needs it, without picking the phone up.

@unlockPitchMac.description: macOS: the locked phone's card when no PIN is saved for it, above the button Save PIN…. The card is in a narrow side panel.

unlockPitchOther: Save its PIN and you can unlock it from this computer when an agent needs it, without picking the phone up.

@unlockPitchOther.description: Linux: the locked phone's card when no PIN is saved for it, above the button Save PIN…. The card is in a narrow side panel.

unlockPitchWindows: Save its PIN and you can unlock it from this computer with Windows Hello when an agent needs it, without picking the phone up.

@unlockPitchWindows.description: Windows: the locked phone's card when no PIN is saved for it, above the button Save PIN…. The card is in a narrow side panel.
